Let Z_1=Z_2=Z with Z distributed as N(0,100). Thus both noises have the required common density, although they are dependent. Fixed tie-breaking is irrelevant: M(X)=1 and M(X')=2 almost surely. At t=0 the two point masses have H_1=1. For Gaussian marginals, the largest H_1 over shifts at distance at most 2 is their total variation delta_2(0)=2 Phi(0.1)-1. Moreover Phi(0.1)-1/2=integral_0^0.1 phi(u)du < 0.1/sqrt(2 pi)<0.04, so 2 delta_2(0)<0.16<1. Hence H_1(M(X)||M(X'))=1>2 delta_2(0), disproving the asserted bound while preserving every other assumption.

full_proof: Choose eta=0, gamma=1/2, and epsilon=log 2, all in the retained domains. On neighboring X,X', let one run Q output quality 1 with probabilities 2/3 and 1/3 respectively, and rank 1 above 0. The probabilities of each binary outcome have ratios at most 2 in both directions, so Q is epsilon-DP. For the stated log-series K law, its probability generating function is g(z)=sum_{k>=1}(z/2)^k/(k log 2)=-log(1-z/2)/log 2. The selected output is 0 exactly when all K runs output 0. Therefore its probabilities on X and X' are g(1/3)=log(6/5)/log 2 and g(2/3)=log(3/2)/log 2. Their X'-to-X ratio is log(3/2)/log(6/5)>2 because 3/2>(6/5)^2=36/25. This exceeds exp((eta+1)epsilon)=2, so the claimed pure-DP conclusion fails.

Its two output laws are identical, so it is (0,0)-DP and therefore is (epsilon,0)-DP in both directions. For identical laws P=Q, the constraint E_P[phi]<=alpha also gives E_Q[phi]<=alpha, and equality is attainable by a constant randomized test; hence T[P,P](alpha)=1-alpha. In particular T[P,P](0)=1. Under the mutated displayed definition, however, f_{epsilon,0}(0)=max{0,1,e^epsilon}=2. Consequently T[P,P](0)=1<2, so even this perfectly private mechanism is not f_{epsilon,0}-DP. This directly disproves the claimed equivalence without changing the test class, neighbor relation, or either directed requirement.
